title: LIVE NOW: CPI DATA INFLATION REPORT OCT. 2026
speaker: Ricky Gutierrez

macro_themes.view: September CPI came in hotter than expected (3.7% headline, 2.6% core), so a market sell-off is a rational reaction.
Energy, especially fuel oil, is the biggest inflation contributor because of Middle East / Strait of Hormuz escalation and Russia sanctions.
Speculative, irrational valuations are only supported in irrational times and crash hardest when markets sell off.

calls.condition: We'll see if the sell-off continues into the open after the hot CPI; trade the 742-746 range extremes
calls.reason: Hot CPI justifies a pullback; prior day's range was 742-746 and he likes fading overbought/oversold extremes.
calls.quote: at least at this point now we're retesting same previous lows. We'll see if the sell-off continues

calls.condition: Buy near the ~900 support lows and sell into the 1,000-1,100 highs; support can break if markets keep selling off
calls.reason: Low P/E, huge revenue and profit amid a memory shortage; has repeatedly bounced from ~900 back to 1,000-1,100. Risk is memory cyclicality and future competition.
calls.quote: anytime that it sells off to the lows of 900, I've really enjoyed buying those lows and allowing it to recover

calls.condition: If markets begin to sell off, speculative names like NBIS should crash hardest
calls.reason: Calls it a gimmick with tiny earnings versus a ~$56B market cap; speculative valuation only holds in irrational markets.
calls.quote: I think you're absolutely crazy if you want to invest in in NBIS from the 200 to the 250 range.

calls.condition: Would only own a small position, prepared for it to get worse before better; wait for a possible gap down for entry
calls.reason: Near a 12-year low, P/E ~17 and 38% upside to fair value, but revenue no longer growing; testing prior resistance at 36.
calls.quote: The cheap can always get cheaper... It could have a gap down where we might want to be patient with that early entry.

calls.reason: Volatile with no clear direction mid-range; lagging tech with a 34 P/E, so not a good investment in his view.
calls.quote: This would not make sense as a good investment for me

notes: Date not stated; CPI (September data) release morning. The AI assistant on stream also quoted 10y at 5.19% and oil ~95, not host views. He called NBIS a 'fusion energy company', apparently confusing it with another name. RDDT long-term bearish is a soft reading of 'not a good investment'.
